iut_type: End Product (Nippon Seimitsu Sokki blood pressure monitor, KAGA FEI module with Nordic SoftDevice), legacy Subset ID QDID reference no longer valid under the post-2024 registration system
customer_question: We want to register referencing a PHY Layer QDID from KAGA FEI, plus a Link Layer and Host Layer QDID that are each listed as a 'subset of' a Nordic Semiconductor QDID (138610) -- is this combination of references still usable for a new registration?
question_variants: Can a legacy 'Subset of' QDID reference still be used for a brand-new registration under the current system?
If a legacy Subset reference can't be used, is there an alternative way to achieve the same registration outcome?
actual_issue: The customer's candidate registration references included a Link Layer and Host Layer QDID that were each registered as a 'subset of' a separate, broader Nordic Semiconductor QDID under the legacy (pre-July-2024) registration system -- but the registration system that took effect July 1, 2024 no longer allows referencing this kind of legacy Subset ID at all, requiring an alternative reference to be found for the same underlying SoftDevice version.
plain_english_explanation: The customer's proposed PHY Layer reference (from KAGA FEI) was fine on its own, but the Link Layer and Host Layer references were both declared as a 'subset of' a separate Nordic QDID (138610) under the old registration system's Subset ID mechanism -- a referencing method the new system (effective July 1, 2024) no longer supports. Rather than telling the customer no solution existed, the consultant searched for a different, properly-registered (non-subset) QDID implementing the same underlying Nordic SoftDevice version and revision (S112, v7.2.0) that the customer's product actually used, and found one. By referencing that QDID's Link Layer and Host Layer components instead of the disallowed Subset references, combined with the KAGA FEI PHY Layer reference, the new registration could proceed with the customer's intended outcome fully preserved -- no functional difference to the customer, just a different (currently-valid) reference QDID achieving the same result.
consultant_answer: Your PHY Layer reference is fine, but the Link Layer and Host Layer references you provided are each a 'subset of' a separate Nordic QDID -- and the registration system in effect since July 1, 2024 no longer allows referencing that kind of legacy Subset ID. The good news: I found a different, properly-registered QDID implementing the same Nordic SoftDevice version (S112, v7.2.0) your product actually uses. We'll reference that QDID's Link Layer and Host Layer instead, combined with your KAGA FEI PHY Layer reference -- this achieves exactly the registration outcome you wanted, just through a currently-valid reference path.
decision_logic: When a customer's candidate reference QDID uses a legacy 'subset of' declaration that the current registration system no longer supports, search for an alternative, properly-registered QDID implementing the same underlying chipset/SoftDevice version and revision, rather than concluding no solution exists -- the goal is to preserve the customer's intended registration outcome through a currently-valid reference path.
final_recommendation: When reviewing a customer's proposed reference QDIDs, check whether any of them rely on a legacy Subset ID mechanism that the current registration system has discontinued, and proactively search for a same-SoftDevice-version alternative reference before reporting back to the customer, so the response includes a solution rather than just a problem.
risk_if_done_wrong: Simply telling the customer their proposed Subset ID reference is no longer valid, without searching for an alternative achieving the same outcome, would have stalled the registration unnecessarily or forced the customer into a more expensive path (such as fresh testing) when a like-for-like alternative reference was available.
